subject.title: TUI: Add config support for --deliver flag default

question: Should OpenClaw add a persistent `tui.deliver` config key for the default `openclaw tui --deliver` behavior, or keep delivery as an explicit launch flag only?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but OpenClaw policy treats config/default additions as product and compatibility-sensitive surfaces that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Approve narrow config default
options.body: Add a documented `tui.deliver` boolean, keep explicit CLI flags authoritative, and cover config/default/override behavior with focused tests.

options.title: Keep flag-only behavior
options.body: Decline the new config surface and rely on `openclaw tui --deliver`, aliases, and current docs now that the adjacent abort hang is fixed.

options.title: Choose a different TUI UX
options.body: Prefer an in-TUI setting, default flip, or another delivery model instead of adding an `openclaw.json` key.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow config default
recommendation.body: Add a documented `tui.deliver` boolean, keep explicit CLI flags authoritative, and cover config/default/override behavior with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The initial TUI/default behavior traces to `steipete`, making this the best available routing candidate for the config/product choice.
